html:
Quiriguá was a small Maya city in the Motagua valley of eastern Guatemala. On 3 May 738 its ruler, K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat, captured and beheaded Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil, the king of Copán, its powerful overlord.

The victory freed Quiriguá from Copán, about fifty kilometres away, and brought it control of trade along the river, including jade. Its king celebrated by raising huge carved stone monuments. Stela E, over ten metres tall, is one of the largest free-standing stones carved by the Maya, and boulders carved as animals called zoomorphs carry long texts in Maya script.

Its texts tell the story of the war, part of the rivalries of the Maya city-states. It became a World Heritage Site in 1981, and its stones were among the first to be studied by scholars of Maya writing in Guatemala.
